recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. I have used their teas and tinctures on an almost daily basis for years now. Kyle is a great friend of InnerVerse and has appeared on the channel more times than I can count. These products work, not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

recFdBmTf1pJJOP6S.Body: LotusWei provides amazing and transformative plant essence elixirs, using one of nature's most gentle and beautiful elements: the flowers themselves. I use LotusWei Elixirs to give me an edge with psychic & energetic sensitivity, discernment, and life force coherence. In other words, LotusWei Elixirs help me be a better podcaster and Biofield Tuner. Benefits accumulate over long term use!

recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Sound as a Model of Coherence", "body": "Chance opened with a slideshow on sound healing and credited Eileen McKusick as the pioneer he followed. He argued that the practitioner does not fix anyone but offers a coherent tone for the body to copy and self tune, and he pointed to synchronizing metronomes as an example of nature's self organization. He said any coherent tone could work and that light, sound and electricity sit on one spectrum. He praised the weighted Sonic Slider fork, which he said was tuned to the Schumann resonance times 12, while cautioning that he could not promise results."}, {"title": "The Biofield as Aura and Mind", "body": "Chance read Eileen McKusick's biofield anatomy hypothesis, which described the biofield as an electromagnetic medium around the body that stores memory. He explained it as the aura, a bubble extending about six feet around the body, and argued that the mind extends beyond the brain, which he compared to a router and perceptual organ. He described experiences as filed to the left or right of the body, with distance from the body matching the age at which they happened. He stressed that this was a conceptual framework and mental scaffolding, not an absolute map."}, {"title": "Reintegrating Fragments Back to the Core", "body": "Chance described sweeping a sounding fork through a person's field until he noticed a change in the tone, then striking it repeatedly at that spot and sweeping the energy back toward the central column. He called stuck pockets compartmentalized or frozen light and said the work could address what seemed like attachments without labeling them. He said he considered this soul retrieval and that the benefit lasted only if the person also changed their mindset. He added that the work functioned remotely through a shared agreement and suggested a future episode on entities."}, {"title": "Mudra, Agreement, and the Group Tune Up", "body": "Before the group session, Chance introduced the Varuna Mudra from a new deck of 72 mudras, touching the pinky and thumb pads together. He then set out his opening agreement that the higher self guides the process and that spirit helpers guard the space. Moving to his massage table of crystals and candles, he spent about half an hour with tuning forks, starting at the earth star and root and rising through each chakra to a halo point above the crown, offering affirmations along the way."}, {"title": "The Key of Destiny for 2022", "body": "Chance laid out his eight card Key of Destiny spread for the new year, starting with I Ching coins that gave Dispersion, number 59. He read it as a call to restore circulation and honest communication, balanced by levity. The Three of Cups reversed, Five of Wands, brown bear, Nine of Wands, Empress and Tower followed, and he said the Tower meant listeners were the lightning bolt. He said the outcome card, Conflict, meant truth telling would stir friction, urged taking time out, and stressed that he was not fortune telling."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Let's kick off 2022 with sound minds! Join me for a brief explanation of sound healing modalities, followed by a group tune-up session.
